Ankle: The joint connecting the foot and leg, composed of the tibia, fibula, and talus.
Cervical Spine: The upper seven vertebrae of the spine, forming the neck region.
Chest: The thoracic cavity containing the heart, lungs, and major blood vessels.
Elbow: The hinge joint between the upper arm and forearm, involving the humerus, radius, and ulna.
Finger: One of the five digits of the hand, composed of phalanges.
Foot: The lower extremity of the leg, containing 26 bones including the tarsals and metatarsals.
Forearm: The region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist.
Hand: The distal part of the upper limb, containing the carpals, metacarpals, and phalanges.
Hip: The ball-and-socket joint connecting the femur to the pelvis.
Humerus: The long bone of the upper arm, connecting the shoulder to the elbow.
Knee: The largest joint in the body, connecting the femur, tibia, and patella.
Leg: The region of the lower limb between the knee and the ankle.
Lumbar Spine: The five lower vertebrae of the spine, supporting the weight of the upper body.
Pelvis: The bony structure at the base of the spine, connecting the spine to the lower limbs.
Shoulder: The ball-and-socket joint formed by the humerus and scapula.
Sinus: Air-filled cavities within the skull bones surrounding the nasal cavity.
Skull: The bony structure encasing and protecting the brain.
Thigh: The region of the lower limb between the hip and the knee, containing the femur.
Tibia: The larger of the two bones in the lower leg, commonly called the shinbone.
Toe: One of the five digits of the foot.
Wrist: The joint between the forearm and the hand, composed of eight carpal bones.
Spine: The vertebral column consisting of 33 vertebrae protecting the spinal cord.
